title: Keyboard Shortcuts
summary: One consolidated bank of Windows, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, browser and function-key shortcuts. The syllabus names keyboard shortcuts explicitly, and 2-4 of the 20 CKT questions are pure shortcut recall, so these are the cheapest marks in the module.

subtopics.title: Windows 10/11 and File Explorer shortcuts
subtopics.concept: The **Windows key** (Win) controls the desktop itself. Most Win shortcuts use the **first letter** of the job: E for Explorer, L for Lock, R for Run. Learn also the security pair **Ctrl+Shift+Esc** and **Ctrl+Alt+Del**, the File Explorer keys, and Alt+Tab and Alt+F4.

tricks.title: First-letter rule
tricks.body: E is Explorer, L is Lock, R is Run, D is Desktop, S is Search, I is settIngs. The letter hints at the job.

tricks.title: Direct vs menu
tricks.body: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager straight away. Ctrl+Alt+Del first opens a menu, and Task Manager is one option there.

example.q: Which shortcut opens Task Manager directly, with no menu first?

mistakes.right: Win+M minimises. Win+Shift+M restores.

mistakes.wrong: Using Ctrl+Alt+Del to open Task Manager directly.
mistakes.right: It opens a menu. Ctrl+Shift+Esc is the direct key.
Alt+F4 closes the program. Ctrl+F4 closes only the document.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking Delete removes a file permanently.
mistakes.right: Delete sends it to the Recycle Bin. Shift+Delete removes it permanently.

mistakes.wrong: Using Win+R to lock the computer.
mistakes.right: Win+L locks. Win+R opens the Run box.

subtopics.notes:
### The Win key family
The **Win key** is the flag key between Ctrl and Alt. Most Win shortcuts use the first letter of the action.

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Win** | Open or close the Start menu |
| **Win+D** | Show the desktop. Press again to bring the windows back |
| **Win+E** | Open File Explorer |
| **Win+L** | **Lock** the computer |
| **Win+R** | Open the **Run** box, where you type cmd, calc or notepad |
| **Win+I** | Open Settings |
| **Win+S** | Open Search |
| **Win+M** | Minimise all windows |
| **Win+Shift+M** | Restore the minimised windows |
| **Win+Tab** | Task view. Shows all windows and virtual desktops |
| **Win+Left / Right / Up / Down** | Snap a window to half or a corner of the screen |
| **Win+PrtScn** | Save a screenshot in the Pictures folder |
| **Win+Shift+S** | Snip a chosen part of the screen |
| **Win+V** | Clipboard history |

> **Watch:** Win+D toggles. Win+M only minimises. Win+Shift+M is needed to restore.

### The security pair
| Combination | What appears |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+Shift+Esc** | **Task Manager** directly. This is the fastest route |
| **Ctrl+Alt+Del** | A full-screen menu with Lock, Switch user, Sign out and Task Manager |
| **Alt+F4** | Closes the active program |

> **Tip:** On the desktop with no program open, Alt+F4 opens the Shut Down box.

### File Explorer keys
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+Shift+N** | New folder |
| **F2** | Rename the selected item |
| **Alt+Enter** | Properties of the selected item |
| **Alt+Up arrow** | Go up one folder level |
| **Delete** | Send to the Recycle Bin |
| **Shift+Delete** | Delete permanently, skipping the Recycle Bin |
| **Ctrl+A** | Select everything |

### Switching and closing windows
- **Alt+Tab** switches between open windows. Hold Alt and tap Tab.
- **Win+D** or **Win+M** clears the screen to the desktop.
- **Win+arrow keys** park a window on half the screen. This is good for comparing two documents.
- **Alt+F4** closes the whole program. **Ctrl+F4** closes only one document inside it.

> **Rule:** Read the verb in the question: switch, close, open or lock. Then pick the key family.

### How questions sound
| The question says | Answer |
|---|---|
| Opens File Explorer | Win+E |
| Locks the computer | Win+L |
| Opens the Run dialog box | Win+R |
| Opens Task Manager directly | Ctrl+Shift+Esc |
| Switches between open programs | Alt+Tab |
| Closes the active program | Alt+F4 |
| Creates a new folder | Ctrl+Shift+N |
| Renames the selected file | F2 |

subtopics.title: Universal Ctrl keys and MS Word shortcuts
subtopics.concept: A group of **Ctrl keys** works in almost every Windows program: N, O, S, P, X, C, V, Z, Y, A and F. Formatting keys are mainly for Word. Some keys have **double lives**, such as Ctrl+H, Ctrl+D and Ctrl+Shift+N. The app named in the question decides the answer.

tricks.title: N-O-S-P and X-C-V
tricks.body: New, Open, Save, Print are N, O, S, P. Cut, Copy, Paste are X, C, V. Undo and Redo are Z and Y.

tricks.title: App decides
tricks.body: Ctrl+H is Replace in Word and History in a browser. Look for the app name in the question before choosing.

example.q: In a web browser, Ctrl+H opens:
steps: In Word it would be Replace.
In a browser it opens History.

mistakes.right: Ctrl+Z is Undo. Ctrl+Y is Redo.
Ctrl+C is Copy. Centre is Ctrl+E.
In a browser Ctrl+H opens History.
Ctrl+W closes a document or tab. Alt+F4 closes the program.
Ctrl+2 is double. Ctrl+5 is 1.5.

subtopics.notes:
### The universal Ctrl keys
These keys work in nearly every Windows app.

| Key | Action | Key | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ctrl+N** | New file | **Ctrl+O** | Open |
| **Ctrl+S** | Save | **Ctrl+P** | Print |
| **Ctrl+Z** | **Undo** | **Ctrl+Y** | Redo |
| **Ctrl+X** | Cut | **Ctrl+C** | Copy |
| **Ctrl+V** | Paste | **Ctrl+A** | Select all |
| **Ctrl+F** | Find | **Ctrl+W** | Close the document or tab |
| **Ctrl+K** | Insert hyperlink | **Ctrl+B, I, U** | Bold, italic, underline |

Letter logic: X looks like scissors, so it cuts. V looks like a paste arrow. Z takes you back. A means all.

### Formatting keys
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| Ctrl+B / I / U | Bold / italic / underline |
| **Ctrl+L / E / R / J** | Left / centre / right / justify |
| **Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+2 / Ctrl+5** | Single / double / 1.5 line spacing |
| **Ctrl+Shift+D** | Double underline |
| **Shift+F3** | Cycles the case of selected text |

> **Tip:** C is taken by Copy, so Centre borrows E from "cEntre". Spacing uses the number itself, and 5 stands for 1.5.

### Find, replace and go to
- **Ctrl+F** opens Find. In Word it opens the Navigation pane. In a browser it finds text on the page.
- **Ctrl+H** is **Replace** in Word and Excel.
- **Ctrl+G** and **F5** open Go To in Word.
- **Ctrl+Home** jumps to the start of the document. **Ctrl+End** jumps to the end.

### Undo and friends
- **Ctrl+Z** undoes the last action. Press again to undo more.
- **Ctrl+Y** redoes it.
- **Ctrl+S** saves. Save often.
- **F12** is Save As in Office programs.

### The double-life table
| Key | Word / Excel | Browser | Explorer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ctrl+H | **Replace** | History | none |
| Ctrl+D | Font box (Word) or fill down (Excel) | **Bookmark** | none |
| Ctrl+Shift+N | none | Incognito window | **New folder** |
| Ctrl+F | Find | Find on page | Search box |
| Ctrl+W | Close document | Close tab | Close window |

### Moving and selecting text
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+Left / Right arrow** | Move one word left or right |
| **Shift+Arrow** | Select one character or line at a time |
| **Ctrl+Shift+Arrow** | Select one word at a time |
| **Home / End** | Go to the start or end of the line |
| **Ctrl+Backspace** | Delete the word before the cursor |

> **Rule:** Read the app named in the question first. It changes the answer for half of the keys here.

### Copy and paste family
- **Ctrl+C** copies. **Ctrl+X** cuts. **Ctrl+V** pastes.
- Copy leaves the original in place. Cut removes it.
- **Ctrl+Shift+V** pastes without formatting in many programs.
- **Win+V** shows the clipboard history in Windows.

> **Example:** "In MS Excel, Ctrl+D will..." The answer is fill down. In Word it opens the Font box. In a browser it bookmarks the page.

subtopics.title: MS Excel and PowerPoint shortcuts
subtopics.concept: This subtopic collects the shortcuts most asked for **Excel** and **PowerPoint**. In Excel, learn the moving, selecting and data-entry keys. In PowerPoint, learn how to start, run and end a show. Ctrl+D has three different jobs across Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

tricks.title: Space pair
tricks.body: Ctrl+Space selects a column. Shift+Space selects a row.

example.q: Which shortcut selects an entire row in Excel?
steps: A row is selected with the Shift key.

tricks.title: Semicolon pair
tricks.body: Ctrl+; enters the date. Adding Shift enters the time.

tricks.title: Shift means here
tricks.body: F5 starts from the first slide. Shift+F5 starts from the slide you are on.

mistakes.wrong: Using Ctrl+Space to select a row.
mistakes.right: Ctrl+Space selects a column. Shift+Space selects a row.

mistakes.wrong: Starting a show from the current slide with F5.
mistakes.right: F5 starts at the beginning. Shift+F5 starts at the current slide.
Ctrl+; is the date. Ctrl+Shift+; is the time.

mistakes.wrong: Using Ctrl+D in PowerPoint to fill down.
mistakes.right: In PowerPoint it duplicates the slide. Fill down is an Excel action.

mistakes.wrong: Using Ctrl+N to add a slide.
mistakes.right: Ctrl+M adds a slide. Ctrl+N makes a new presentation.

subtopics.notes:
### Excel: moving around
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+Home** | Jump to cell **A1** |
| **Ctrl+End** | Jump to the last used cell |
| **Ctrl+Page Down / Up** | Next / previous **worksheet** |
| **Ctrl+Arrow key** | Edge of the current block of data |
| **F5 / Ctrl+G** | Go To a cell |
| **Ctrl+F** | Find |

### Excel: selecting and editing
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+Space** | Select the whole **column** |
| **Shift+Space** | Select the whole **row** |
| **Ctrl+A** | Select the sheet or data block |
| **F2** | **Edit** the active cell |
| **Alt+Enter** | New line inside one cell |
| **Ctrl+D** | **Fill down** from the cell above |
| **Ctrl+R** | **Fill right** from the cell on the left |
| **Ctrl+;** | Enter today's **date** |
| **Ctrl+Shift+;** | Enter the current **time** |
| **F4** | Cycles reference styles. Also repeats the last action |
| **Ctrl+1** | Format Cells |
| **Ctrl+Shift+L** | Toggle filter |
| **Alt+=** | AutoSum |
| **Shift+F11** | New worksheet |

> **Tip:** Ctrl+Space is a tall thin column. Shift+Space is a flat row.

### PowerPoint: running the show
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **F5** | Start the show from the **beginning** |
| **Shift+F5** | Start from the **current slide** |
| **Esc** | End the show |
| **B** | Black screen. Press again to return |
| **W** | White screen |
| **N, Space, Right arrow** | Next slide |
| **P, Left arrow** | Previous slide |
| **Number + Enter** | Jump to that slide |
| **Ctrl+M** | New slide |
| **Ctrl+D** | Duplicate the current slide |

> **Watch:** Ctrl+D duplicates a slide in PowerPoint. It fills down in Excel. It opens the Font box in Word.

### Formatting keys that carry over
Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+U work in Excel cells and PowerPoint text boxes too. The alignment keys Ctrl+E, Ctrl+L and Ctrl+R also work in PowerPoint text.

### Everyday examples
| You want to... | Press |
|---|---|
| Copy a formula down a column | Ctrl+D |
| Jump to the last cell you filled | Ctrl+End |
| Type an address on two lines in one cell | Alt+Enter between lines |
| Put today's date on a report | Ctrl+; |
| Test one slide without the whole show | Shift+F5 |
| Keep the audience looking at you | B for black screen |

### Shared keys that also work here
- **Ctrl+C**, **Ctrl+X** and **Ctrl+V** copy, cut and paste in both Excel and PowerPoint.
- **Ctrl+Z** and **Ctrl+Y** undo and redo.
- **Ctrl+S** saves and **F12** opens Save As.
- **Ctrl+P** prints when you are editing.

### A ten-second method
1. Read the action in the question.
2. Recall the family: selection uses Space, filling uses D or R, the show uses F5.
3. Remove options that swap row and column, or F5 and Shift+F5.

subtopics.title: Web browser shortcuts (Chrome, Edge, Firefox)
subtopics.concept: Browser shortcuts handle tabs, windows, privacy and history. **Ctrl+T** opens a tab, **Ctrl+W** closes it and **Ctrl+Shift+T** brings it back. Ctrl+H, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+D do different jobs in a browser than in Word or Excel.

tricks.title: Tab trio
tricks.body: T opens a tab, W closes it and Shift+T reopens the one you closed.

example.q: Which shortcut reopens the most recently closed tab?
steps: The undo of that adds Shift and T.

tricks.title: H, J, D
tricks.body: H is History, J is downloads (the next letter) and D is a bookmark (Dog-ear a page).

mistakes.wrong: Reading Ctrl+9 as the ninth tab.
mistakes.right: Ctrl+9 jumps to the last tab.

mistakes.wrong: Using Ctrl+H for Replace in a browser.
mistakes.right: In a browser Ctrl+H is History.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking Incognito hides you from websites.
mistakes.right: It only stops local saving of history and cookies.

mistakes.wrong: Using Ctrl+N for a private window.
mistakes.right: Ctrl+N is a normal new window. Ctrl+Shift+N is private.
F5 reloads. Ctrl+F5 reloads without the cache.

subtopics.notes:
### Tabs
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+T** | New tab |
| **Ctrl+W** (or Ctrl+F4) | Close the current tab |
| **Ctrl+Shift+T** | **Reopen the last closed tab**. This is the undo of Ctrl+W |
| **Ctrl+Tab** | Next tab |
| **Ctrl+Shift+Tab** | Previous tab |
| **Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+8** | Jump to tab 1 to 8 |
| **Ctrl+9** | Jump to the **last** tab |

> **Watch:** Ctrl+9 goes to the last tab. It does not go to the ninth tab.

### Windows and privacy
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Ctrl+N** | New window |
| **Ctrl+Shift+N** | New **Incognito** (Chrome) or **InPrivate** (Edge) window |
| **Ctrl+Shift+P** | Private window in **Firefox** |
| **Ctrl+Shift+Delete** | Open Clear browsing data |

> **Note:** Incognito mode stops the browser from saving history and cookies on that computer. It does not hide your activity from websites or your internet provider.

### Getting around a page
| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| **Alt+Left** | Back |
| **Alt+Right** | Forward |
| **Alt+Home** | Open the home page |
| **F5** | Reload |
| **Ctrl+F5** | Reload and skip the cache |
| **F11** | Full screen on or off |
| **Ctrl+F** | Find on the page |
| **Ctrl+D** | **Bookmark** this page |
| **Ctrl+Shift+B** | Show or hide the bookmarks bar |
| **Ctrl+H** | **History** |
| **Ctrl+J** | **Downloads** |

### Keys with double lives
The same key can do different jobs in a browser and in Office.

| Key | Browser | Word / Excel |
|---|---|---|
| Ctrl+H | **History** | Replace (Word) |
| Ctrl+N | New **window** | New **document** or **workbook** |
| Ctrl+Shift+N | Incognito window | New **folder** (Explorer) |
| Ctrl+D | **Bookmark** | Font box (Word) or fill down (Excel) |
| Ctrl+F | Find on page | Find |

> **Rule:** If the question says "in a web browser", use the browser column.

### Why the browser keys matter
A browser holds many pages at once, and shortcuts save clicks. The tab keys use letters T and W. The private window key adds Shift to N. Learn these first because the exam asks them most.

### Address bar and page keys
- **Ctrl+L** or **F6** puts the cursor in the address bar.
- **Ctrl+P** prints the page.
- **Ctrl+S** saves the page.
- **Ctrl++** zooms in. **Ctrl+-** zooms out. **Ctrl+0** returns to normal zoom.
- **Esc** stops a page that is still loading.

### Everyday examples
| You just... | Do this |
|---|---|
| Closed a tab you still needed | Ctrl+Shift+T |
| Want a private session | Ctrl+Shift+N |
| Lost the bookmarks bar | Ctrl+Shift+B |
| Need a page you visited last week | Ctrl+H |
| Want the file you downloaded | Ctrl+J |
| Have a page stuck on an old version | Ctrl+F5 |

subtopics.title: Function keys F1-F12
subtopics.concept: The **F1 to F12** keys have fixed jobs, but some change with the program. F1 is Help, F2 renames, F5 refreshes or starts a slide show, F7 checks spelling and F12 is Save As. Read the program named in the question.

tricks.title: Alt closes programs
tricks.body: Alt+F4 closes the whole program. Ctrl+F4 closes only the current document or tab.

example.q: Which key closes only the current document, leaving the program open?

tricks.title: Twelve is Save As
tricks.body: F12 opens Save As in Office. In a browser the same key opens developer tools.

mistakes.right: F1 opens Help. F2 renames or edits.
In PowerPoint F5 starts the slide show.
Alt+F4 closes the whole program. Ctrl+F4 closes the document.

mistakes.wrong: Using F10 for the right-click menu.
mistakes.right: Shift+F10 gives the right-click menu.
In browsers F7 turns on caret browsing.

subtopics.notes:
### The F1 to F12 row
| Key | Windows | Office | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** | **Help** | Help | none |
| **F2** | Rename a file | Edit a cell in Excel | none |
| **F3** | Search in Explorer | Shift+F3 changes case in Word | none |
| **F4** | Address bar list | Repeats the last action. Cycles references in Excel | Alt+F4 closes a program |
| **F5** | **Refresh** | Slide show (PowerPoint), Go To (Word) | Ctrl+F5 hard reload |
| **F6** | Moves between screen parts | none | none |
| **F7** | none | **Spelling and grammar** | Caret browsing in browsers |
| **F8** | Safe Mode at start-up (older Windows) | Extend selection | none |
| **F9** | none | Update fields (Word), recalculate (Excel) | Send/Receive (Outlook) |
| **F10** | Activate the menu bar | none | **Shift+F10 is right-click** |
| **F11** | Full screen in browsers | Chart sheet (Excel) | none |
| **F12** | Developer tools in browsers | **Save As** | none |

### Memory hooks
- One is help on demand. Two is the second name, a rename. Five is fresh, a refresh. Seven is for spelling.
- Twelve saves your work under a new name, Save As.
- **Shift+F10** gives the right-click menu. F10 opens the menu bar, and Shift makes it act at your cursor.
- **Alt+F4** closes the program. **Ctrl+F4** closes only the document or tab.

> **Tip:** Say the ladder aloud: help, rename, search, refresh. Stop when you reach the match.

### Same key, different program
| Key | Windows | Word | Excel | PowerPoint | Browser |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F5 | Refresh | Go To | Go To | **Slide show** | Reload |
| F2 | Rename | none | Edit cell | none | none |
| F7 | none | Spelling | Spelling | Spelling | Caret browsing |
| F12 | none | Save As | Save As | Save As | Developer tools |
| F11 | none | none | Chart sheet | none | Full screen |

> **Watch:** F5 in PowerPoint runs the show. F5 on the desktop refreshes.

### Modifier plus F key
- **Shift+F3** cycles the case in Word.
- **Shift+F5** starts the show from the current slide.
- **Shift+F7** opens the thesaurus in Word.
- **Shift+F11** adds a worksheet in Excel.
- **Ctrl+F4** closes a document. **Alt+F4** closes a program.
- **Ctrl+F5** reloads a browser page and skips the cache.

### A quick ladder to say aloud
F1 help. F2 rename. F3 search. F4 repeat. F5 refresh. F6 next pane. F7 spelling. F8 select or Safe Mode. F9 update. F10 menu. F11 full screen. F12 Save As.

> **Note:** The same ladder works for most exam questions. Then check which program the question names.

### Everyday examples
| You want to... | Press |
|---|---|
| Learn what a button does | F1 |
| Rename a file | F2 |
| Reload a misbehaving page | F5 |
| Fix red underlines | F7 |
| Save with a different name | F12 |
| Open the menu without the mouse | F10 |

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which shortcut opens File Explorer / creates a new folder / locks the screen?', 'the shortcut to close the active program is'.
pyqPatterns.approach: Recall by first-letter logic on the Win-key row (Win+E Explorer, Win+L Lock, Win+R Run) and by family: Alt+F4 closes a program, Alt+Tab switches, Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager directly while Ctrl+Alt+Del shows the security screen first. Eliminate options whose modifier contradicts the verb.

example.q: Which shortcut opens File Explorer?
example.solution: Win+E — E for Explorer. Win+X is the power-user menu, Win+P projection.

pyqPatterns.pattern: 'What does key X do' reverse recall
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Ctrl+H in Word opens…', 'Ctrl+D in Word/Excel does what?', 'What is the function of Ctrl+Y?' — the key is given, the action is asked.
pyqPatterns.approach: Reverse the table: key first, then app. Ctrl+H = Replace in Word but History in a browser; Ctrl+D = Font dialog in Word, fill down in Excel, duplicate in PowerPoint, bookmark in a browser; Ctrl+Y = redo. Always read which application the stem names before answering.

example.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+D opens the:
example.solution: Font dialog box — not duplicate (PowerPoint) and not fill-down (Excel).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'F1 is used for', 'which key refreshes the page?', 'spell check runs on which function key?', 'which F-key starts the slideshow?'.
pyqPatterns.approach: Ladder recall: F1 help, F2 rename/edit cell, F3 search, F5 refresh/show/Go To, F7 spelling, F12 Save As (Office) or developer tools (browser). Then let the app decide: F5 in PowerPoint is the show, F5 on the desktop is refresh.

example.q: Which function key runs the spelling and grammar check?
example.solution: F7 — in Word, Excel and PowerPoint alike.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'F5 in MS PowerPoint starts… but on the desktop it…', 'Ctrl+D has different uses in Word, Excel and a browser', statement questions mixing apps.
pyqPatterns.approach: Build the cross-table: F5 = refresh/reload (Windows, browsers) vs slideshow (PPT) vs Go To (Word); F12 = Save As (Office) vs dev tools (browser); Ctrl+Shift+N = Incognito (browser) vs new folder (Explorer); Ctrl+H = Replace (Word) vs History (browser). The app named in the stem picks the answer.

example.q: F5 in MS PowerPoint starts the slideshow. What does F5 do on the Windows desktop?
example.solution: It refreshes the desktop or active window — same key, different job per application.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Ctrl+H in a browser opens…', 'shortcut for Incognito mode', 'which shortcut reopens a closed tab?', 'Ctrl+D in Chrome does what?'.
pyqPatterns.approach: Browser column: Ctrl+T new tab, Ctrl+W close, Ctrl+Shift+T reopen closed, Ctrl+Shift+N Incognito (Firefox = Ctrl+Shift+P), Alt+Left back, Ctrl+D bookmark, Ctrl+H history, Ctrl+J downloads, Ctrl+Shift+Delete clear data. Check the stem says 'browser' — Ctrl+H is Replace in Word and Ctrl+Shift+N is a new folder in Explorer.

example.q: In a web browser, Ctrl+H opens:
example.solution: Browsing history — the same keys open Find and Replace in MS Word.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: List A has shortcuts (or keys), List B has actions; options are four mappings like 'A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3'.
pyqPatterns.approach: Solve the sure pairs first: bold Ctrl+B, undo Ctrl+Z, Task Manager Ctrl+Shift+Esc, new folder Ctrl+Shift+N, slideshow F5. Strike every option mispairing a certain pair, then match the leftovers by elimination.

example.q:
Match: A. Ctrl+Shift+N  B. Alt+F4  C. Win+E  D. Ctrl+Shift+Esc
1. Close program 2. New folder 3. Task Manager 4. File Explorer
example.solution: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3 — each certain pair removes two wrong options at once.

solvedExamples.q: Which Windows shortcut locks the computer immediately, so a password or PIN is needed to return?
solvedExamples.solution: Win+L locks the workstation and shows the lock screen. Win+D shows the desktop and Win+M minimises all windows, but neither locks anything. Ctrl+Alt+L is not a Windows lock key.

solvedExamples.q: Pressing Shift+F10 in Windows has the same effect as:
solvedExamples.solution: Shift+F10 opens the shortcut (context) menu for the selected item, exactly like a right mouse click. F10 on its own activates the menu bar.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Shift+F10 = right-click; F10 alone = menu bar.

solvedExamples.q: In MS Excel, which shortcut moves to the NEXT worksheet in the workbook?
solvedExamples.solution: Ctrl+PageDown moves to the next sheet and Ctrl+PageUp to the previous one. Shift+F11 inserts a new worksheet rather than moving to one. Ctrl+Tab switches between open workbooks.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Page keys turn the workbook's pages: Down = next, Up = previous.

solvedExamples.q: In MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint, the F12 key opens the:
solvedExamples.solution: F12 opens Save As in all Office apps. Ctrl+P prints, F1 opens Help and F7 runs the spelling check.
solvedExamples.shortcut: F12 is at the end of the row, and you Save As at the end of your work.

practice.q: Which shortcut minimises all open windows to show the desktop, and restores them when pressed again?
practice.solution: Win+D toggles the desktop: the first press hides every window and the second press brings them back. Win+E opens File Explorer, and Win+Tab/Alt+Tab switch windows.

practice.q: In Windows 10/11, pressing Win+V opens:
practice.solution: Win+V shows clipboard history, a list of recently copied items you can paste again (it must be switched on the first time). Run is Win+R and voice typing is Win+H.
practice.shortcut: Ctrl+V pastes one item; Win+V opens the whole paste history.

practice.q: Which shortcut lets you drag a box to capture a chosen part of the screen with the Snipping Tool?
practice.solution: Win+Shift+S opens the screen snip toolbar (rectangle, free-form, window, full screen). Alt+PrtScn captures only the active window, Win+P changes display projection, and Ctrl+Shift+S is Save As in some apps.
practice.shortcut: S = Snip; Win+Shift makes it a system-wide snip.

practice.q: Which key combination switches between open application windows?
practice.solution: Alt+Tab cycles through all open windows. Ctrl+Tab switches tabs inside one application, Shift+Tab moves focus backwards, and Alt+F4 closes the window.
practice.shortcut: Alt = Active window: Alt+Tab switches it, Alt+F4 closes it.

practice.q: The Run dialog box, used to launch programs such as 'cmd' or 'calc' by name, opens with:
practice.solution: Win+R opens Run. Win+X opens the Quick Link (power user) menu. Ctrl+R reloads a browser page and does Fill Right in Excel.

practice.q: In Windows File Explorer, which shortcut creates a new folder in the current location?
practice.solution: Ctrl+Shift+N creates a new folder in Explorer. Plain Ctrl+N opens a new Explorer window. In Chrome, Ctrl+Shift+N opens an incognito window.
practice.shortcut: Ctrl+N = new window; add Shift for a new folder.

practice.q: A file is selected in File Explorer. Pressing Alt+Enter will:
practice.solution: Alt+Enter opens the Properties dialog (size, location, dates, attributes). Enter opens the file, F2 renames it and Delete sends it to the Recycle Bin.

practice.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+J applies which alignment to the selected paragraph?
practice.solution: Ctrl+J justifies text so both margins are straight. Left is Ctrl+L, centre is Ctrl+E and right is Ctrl+R.

practice.q: Which shortcut sets double line spacing in MS Word?
practice.solution: Ctrl+2 gives double spacing, Ctrl+1 single spacing and Ctrl+5 1.5 spacing. Ctrl+D opens the Font dialog.
practice.shortcut: The digit is the spacing; 5 means 1.5.

practice.q: The Find and Replace dialog in MS Word opens directly on the Replace tab with:
practice.solution: Ctrl+H opens Replace. Ctrl+F opens the Navigation (find) pane, Ctrl+G opens Go To, and Ctrl+R right-aligns text.
practice.shortcut: H = cHange/replace in Word (but History in a browser).

practice.q: In MS Excel, pressing Ctrl+Space selects:
practice.solution: Ctrl+Space selects the whole column of the active cell and Shift+Space selects the whole row. Ctrl+A selects the data region, or the whole sheet if pressed again.
practice.shortcut: Ctrl and Column both start with C; Shift+Space = row.

practice.q: A value is in A2 and the range A2:A10 is selected. Which shortcut copies A2 into A3:A10?
practice.solution: Ctrl+D (Fill Down) copies the top cell of the selection into the cells below it. Ctrl+R fills right, Ctrl+C only copies to the clipboard, and Ctrl+E is Flash Fill.

practice.q: In MS Excel, the shortcut Shift+F3 opens the:
practice.solution: In Excel, Shift+F3 opens Insert Function (the fx dialog). The change-case meaning belongs to MS Word, which is the trap. Name Manager is Ctrl+F3.
practice.shortcut: Same key, different app: Word = case, Excel = function.

practice.q: In Chrome and Edge, which shortcut opens the 'Clear browsing data' dialog?
practice.solution: Ctrl+Shift+Delete opens the dialog for clearing history, cookies and cached files. Shift+Delete is permanent file deletion in File Explorer, not a browser command.
practice.shortcut: Ctrl+Shift = the strong version; the strongest delete wipes browsing data.

practice.q: Which shortcut takes a web browser back to the previously visited page?
practice.solution: Alt+Left goes back and Alt+Right goes forward. Alt+Home opens the home page, and Ctrl+Left moves the cursor one word left in a text box.

practice.q: Which shortcut opens **File Explorer**?
practice.solution: **Win+E** opens File Explorer (E for Explorer). Win+X opens the power-user menu; Win+P handles projection.

practice.q: The **Run** dialog, where you can type 'cmd' or 'calc', opens with —
practice.solution: **Win+R** = Run — type a program name and press Enter.

practice.q: Pressing **Win+D** and then pressing it again will —
options: Show the desktop, then restore the open windows
practice.solution: **Win+D toggles**: first press hides all windows to show the desktop, second press brings them back. Win+M, by contrast, only minimises.

practice.q: Which shortcut captures a **selected part of the screen** with the Snipping overlay?
practice.solution: **Win+Shift+S** opens the snip bar — drag to capture a rectangle, window or full screen.

practice.q: Windows **clipboard history**, which remembers several recent copied items, opens with —
practice.solution: **Win+V** shows the clipboard history (paste any of your recent copies). Plain Ctrl+V pastes only the latest item.

practice.q: Which key combination opens **Task Manager directly**?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+Esc** jumps straight to Task Manager. Ctrl+Alt+Del first shows the security screen.
practice.shortcut: Esc = escape straight into Task Manager.

practice.q: Pressing **Ctrl+Alt+Del** shows —
options: The Windows security screen (Lock, Switch user, Sign out, Task Manager)
practice.solution: Ctrl+Alt+Del opens the **security screen**; Task Manager is one option on it. For the direct route, use Ctrl+Shift+Esc.
practice.shortcut: Three keys, one menu, then your pick.

practice.q: In File Explorer, which shortcut creates a **new folder**?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+N** makes a new folder in the current location. Plain Ctrl+N opens a new window.
practice.shortcut: Shift raises the stakes: window → folder.

practice.q: Which key **renames** a selected file in File Explorer?
practice.solution: **F2** renames the selected item — give it a second name.

practice.q: With a file selected, **Alt+Enter** shows —
options: The file in a new window
practice.solution: **Alt+Enter** opens Properties (size, dates, attributes) — the keyboard way of right-clicking and choosing Properties.

practice.q: You are deep inside C:\Users\Me\Photos\2026. Which shortcut moves **up one folder** (to Photos)?
practice.solution: **Alt+Up** climbs to the parent folder. Alt+Left goes *back* to wherever you came from — not the same thing.
practice.shortcut: Up = one level up; Left = back in history.

practice.q: Which combination **switches between open application windows**?
practice.solution: **Alt+Tab** cycles through open programs (Ctrl+Tab switches tabs inside one app instead).
practice.shortcut: Alt = across apps; Ctrl = across tabs.

practice.q: Which shortcut **closes the active program**?
practice.solution: **Alt+F4** closes the window in front. On the desktop, it opens the shutdown dialog.

practice.q: **Win + Left arrow** does what to the current window?
options: Snaps it to the left half of the screen
Moves it to another monitor only
practice.solution: **Snap**: Win+Left/Right parks the window on that half; Win+Up maximises; Win+Down restores or minimises.

practice.q: While holding **Alt**, pressing **Shift+Tab** in the switcher —
options: Moves through the windows in the reverse direction
practice.solution: Shift reverses direction in almost every Windows cycle — in Alt+Tab it walks the window list backwards.

practice.q: Which shortcut **pastes** copied content?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+V** pastes; Ctrl+X cuts, Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+P prints.

practice.q: **Ctrl+Y** in MS Word —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Y = redo** (it can also repeat the last action). Undo is Ctrl+Z.

practice.q: To **select the entire document** in one stroke, press —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+A** = select **A**ll — the whole document or every cells/rows in the active region.

practice.q: Which shortcut **inserts a hyperlink** in Word or Excel?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+K** opens the hyperlink dialog (K sits next to L for 'link' on the keyboard).

practice.q: Which shortcut makes selected text **bold**?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+B** = bold, Ctrl+I = italic, Ctrl+U = underline — the initial letters.

practice.q: Which shortcut **centres** the selected paragraph in Word?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+E = cEntre.** Ctrl+C is copy; C was taken, so centre borrowed E.

practice.q: The correct set of Word alignment shortcuts is —
practice.solution: **LERJ**: Left, cEntre, Right, Justify.
practice.shortcut: LERJ — left to right across the line.

practice.q: **Shift+F3** in MS Word —
options: Changes the case of selected text (lower/UPPER/Capitalise)
practice.solution: **Shift+F3** cycles the case of the selection in Word — press repeatedly to march lower → UPPER → Capitalise Each Word. (In Excel, plain Shift+F3 opens Insert Function instead.)

practice.q: Which shortcut jumps to the **beginning of the document**?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Home** = document start; **Ctrl+End** = document end.

practice.q: In Word, **Ctrl+G** opens the same dialog as —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+G and F5 both open Go To**, for jumping to a page, section or line number.

practice.q: Which shortcut closes the **current document** without closing the Word application?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+W** (or Ctrl+F4) closes the document window; **Alt+F4** quits the whole program.

practice.q: In **MS Word**, Ctrl+D opens the —
practice.solution: Ctrl+D opens the **Font** dialog in Word. 'Duplicate' belongs to PowerPoint (Ctrl+D duplicates a slide/object); fill-down is Excel's Ctrl+D.
practice.shortcut: Same key, three apps, three jobs.

practice.q: The **Office key that saves with a new name/ location** (Save As) is —
practice.solution: **F12 = Save As** in Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Plain save stays Ctrl+S.

practice.q: Which statement is **correct**?
practice.solution: The undo pair is **Ctrl+Z (undo) / Ctrl+Y (redo)**. The cut-copy pair is Ctrl+X / Ctrl+C; printing is Ctrl+P.
practice.shortcut: Z back, Y forward; X cuts, C copies.

practice.q:
Match the Word shortcut to its effect:
A. Ctrl+J  B. Ctrl+2  C. Shift+F3  D. Ctrl+U
options: A-underline, B-change case, C-double spacing, D-justify
A-justify, B-double spacing, C-change case, D-underline
A-justify, B-change case, C-double spacing, D-underline
A-double spacing, B-justify, C-underline, D-change case
practice.solution: Ctrl+**J** = **J**ustify; Ctrl+**2** = double spacing; Shift+**F3** = case cycling; Ctrl+**U** = **U**nderline.

practice.q: In MS Excel, **Ctrl+Home** moves the cell pointer to —
options: The top of the visible screen
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Home** = A1. Ctrl+End = the last used cell of the sheet.

practice.q: Which shortcut moves to the **next worksheet** in the same workbook?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+PgDn / Ctrl+PgUp** flip through the sheet tabs.
practice.shortcut: Page = the next sheet of the book.

practice.q: In Excel, **Ctrl+End** takes you to —
options: The bottom of the current column only
A new row at the very end
The last used cell of the worksheet
practice.solution: **Ctrl+End** jumps to the bottom-right of the used range — the last cell holding data or formatting.
practice.shortcut: End of what you actually used.

practice.q: Which shortcut selects the **entire row** containing the active cell?
practice.solution: **Shift+Space = row**, Ctrl+Space = column.

practice.q: To select the **entire worksheet** at once, press —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+A** selects all; one press covers the sheet (a second press extends it in older versions).

practice.q: Which key **edits the active cell** in Excel?
practice.solution: **F2** puts the cell in edit mode — the keyboard version of a double-click.

practice.q: While typing in a cell, which shortcut starts a **new line within the same cell**?
practice.solution: **Alt+Enter** inserts a line break inside the cell. Ctrl+Enter fills all selected cells with the entry instead.

practice.q: Which shortcut **copies the contents of the cell above** into the active cell?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+D = fill down** (from the cell above); **Ctrl+R = fill right**.

practice.q: Which shortcut inserts **today's date** into the active cell?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+;** stamps the date; **Ctrl+Shift+;** stamps the current time.

practice.q: Which statement about **F4** in Excel is correct?
options: It cycles a cell reference between absolute, mixed and relative forms
It opens the Format Cells dialog
practice.solution: **F4** toggles absolute/mixed/relative addressing while editing a reference (and repeats the last action outside edit mode). Format Cells is Ctrl+1; saving is Ctrl+S.

practice.q: The shortcut to start a **slide show from the beginning** is —
practice.solution: **F5** runs the show from slide 1; **Shift+F5** starts from the current slide.

practice.q: During a slideshow, pressing **B** turns the screen —
practice.solution: **B = black screen, W = white screen**; press the same key again to bring the slide back.

practice.q: Which shortcut ends a running **slideshow**?
practice.solution: **Esc** ends the show and returns to the editor.

practice.q: Which shortcut starts the slideshow **from the current slide**?
practice.solution: **Shift+F5** previews from the slide you are editing — ideal when polishing one slide.

practice.q: In PowerPoint, **Ctrl+M** —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+M** adds a new slide (M = 'more slides').

practice.q:
Match the Excel shortcut:
A. Ctrl+D  B. Ctrl+R  C. Ctrl+;  D. Alt+Enter
options: A-fill right, B-fill down, C-current time, D-new line in cell
A-fill down, B-fill right, C-current date, D-new line in cell
A-fill down, B-new line in cell, C-current date, D-fill right
A-current date, B-fill right, C-fill down, D-new line in cell
practice.solution: **D down, R right, ; date, Alt+Enter line-break.**

practice.q: Which shortcut opens a **new tab** in a web browser?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+T** = new tab; Ctrl+N = new whole window; Ctrl+Tab = move to the next existing tab.

practice.q: Which shortcut **closes the current browser tab**?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+W** (or Ctrl+F4) closes the tab; Alt+F4 would close the entire browser window.

practice.q: Which shortcut **reopens the last closed tab**?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+T** is the undo of Ctrl+W — it restores recently closed tabs one by one.

practice.q: In a browser, **Ctrl+9** jumps to —
practice.solution: Ctrl+1–8 pick tab numbers 1–8, but **Ctrl+9 always goes to the rightmost (last) tab**, however many are open.

practice.q: Which shortcut opens an **Incognito (private) window** in Chrome/Edge?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+N** — Chrome and Edge. Firefox uses Ctrl+Shift+P.

practice.q: In **Mozilla Firefox**, a private browsing window opens with —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+P** = Private window in Firefox. (The same keys open the Print dialog in Chrome/Edge.)

practice.q: Which shortcut opens the **Clear browsing data** dialog?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+Delete** opens the panel to wipe history, cookies and cache.

practice.q: Which shortcut goes **back to the previous page** in a browser?
practice.solution: **Alt+Left = back, Alt+Right = forward** — history direction keys.

practice.q: **Ctrl+D** in a web browser —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+D = bookmark** ('D for done reading'). Downloads are Ctrl+J.

practice.q: Which shortcut toggles the **bookmarks bar**?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+Shift+B** shows or hides the bookmarks bar; plain Ctrl+B is bold in documents.

practice.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Ctrl+H shows history but Ctrl+H in Word opens Replace
Ctrl+H shows history in every program
Ctrl+D bookmarks a page and duplicates slides in Word
Alt+Home opens the browser's download page
practice.solution: Ctrl+H is **History in browsers, Replace in Word** — same keys, different apps. Ctrl+D duplicates slides in PowerPoint, not Word; the browser home page is Alt+Home (that part of option D is right but its download-page tail is wrong).
practice.shortcut: Same key, three apps, three jobs.

practice.q: In a web browser, **Ctrl+J** opens —
practice.solution: **Ctrl+J = Downloads** list — J for the 'just fetched' files.

practice.q: Which shortcut opens the **browser history** page?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+H = History** in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

practice.q: Which shortcut switches the browser to **full screen**?
practice.solution: **F11** toggles full screen; F5 reloads; F12 opens developer tools.

practice.q:
Match the app to its private-window shortcut:
A. Chrome  B. Edge  C. Firefox
practice.solution: Chrome and Edge (Chromium family) share **Ctrl+Shift+N**; only Firefox uses **Ctrl+Shift+P**.

practice.q: Which function key opens **Help** in most programs?
practice.solution: **F1** is the universal help key — one key, one demand for help.

practice.q: Which function key **renames** a selected file or folder?
practice.solution: **F2** renames in File Explorer and edits the active cell in Excel — a second look at the item.

practice.q: Which function key **refreshes** the desktop or a web page?
practice.solution: **F5** refreshes; Ctrl+F5 reloads even harder (ignoring the cache).

practice.q: Which function key opens the **Save As** dialog in MS Word?
practice.solution: **F12 = Save As** in all Office apps; plain saving stays on Ctrl+S.

practice.q: Pressing **F3** in File Explorer opens —
practice.solution: **F3** opens the search box in File Explorer (in Word, Shift+F3 cycles letter case instead).

practice.q: Which function key runs the **Spelling & Grammar** check in MS Word?
practice.solution: **F7** spells — in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

practice.q: In MS Excel, which key **edits the active cell**?
practice.solution: **F2** puts the cell into edit mode (rename in Explorer, edit in Excel).

practice.q: **Shift+F11** in MS Excel —
practice.solution: **Shift+F11** adds a fresh worksheet; plain **F11** turns the selection into a **chart sheet**.

practice.q: In MS Word, **F5** opens the —
practice.solution: In Word, F5 (like Ctrl+G) opens **Go To** for jumping to a page or line. The slideshow F5 belongs to PowerPoint.
practice.shortcut: F5 by app: Word = go, PPT = show.

practice.q: Which combination **closes the active program**?
practice.solution: **Alt+F4** quits the program; **Ctrl+F4** closes only the current document or tab inside it.

practice.q: **Shift+F10** —
practice.solution: **Shift+F10** = the keyboard's right-click; F10 alone highlights the menu bar.

practice.q: Which combination closes **only the current document**, keeping the application open?
practice.solution: **Ctrl+F4** closes the document window inside the app; **Alt+F4** closes the app itself.
practice.shortcut: Ctrl = close content; Alt = close app.

practice.q: Which pair is **correctly matched**?
options: F10 — activates the menu bar; Shift+F10 — right-click menu
practice.solution: **F10** lights up the menu bar; add **Shift** and it behaves as the right-click at your cursor. Refresh is F5, spellcheck F7, help F1, rename F2.

practice.q: In a web browser, **F12** opens —
practice.solution: F12 flips meaning by app: **Save As in Office, developer tools in browsers**.
practice.shortcut: F12 in a browser = build mode.

practice.q: In MS Excel, **F11** creates —
options: A chart sheet from the selected data
practice.solution: **F11** = chart on its own sheet; **Shift+F11** = new blank worksheet; F11 in a **browser** = full screen.

practice.q: Traditionally, pressing which key **during Windows start-up** entered Safe Mode?
practice.solution: **F8** at boot opened the advanced start-up menu with Safe Mode on older Windows versions — a classic exam fact.

practice.q: Which statement about **F5** is correct?
options: It refreshes a web page and starts the slideshow in PowerPoint
It saves the file in Word
practice.solution: F5 = **refresh/reload** on desktops and browsers, **slideshow** in PowerPoint, **Go To** in Word. Spellcheck is F7; save-as is F12; closing is Alt+F4.

practice.q:
Arrange the function-key ladder correctly:
Help, Rename, Refresh, Save As (Office)
practice.solution: Help = **F1**, rename = **F2**, refresh = **F5**, Save As = **F12**.
